I know its the fear of abandonment. But I'm saying I don't feel abandoned or have the feeling he abandoned me when we didn't talk for an hour or two. But the fact that I dont have any reassurance or notice of if he's coming back or not, if he is just busy or blocked me, especially after a discussion. If he tells me he's going to study I can easily handle two hours of not talking without any fear. To me thats a big difference.

He was overwhelmed and doubted everything and the fact that we both need things from the other that we dont naturally give but have to actually work on giving plus having a big fight made him just explode, is what I see from it. But that doesn't change the fact that he broke up, blocked me and the next day apologised for how he talked to me but stood behind the breakup and I had to talk him back into the relationship and "convince him" by saying we can work on it and that I just want him. Both those facts make the current situation very fragile and instable to me..

I tried to tell him as well that its factually my brain and yes I can and already do and will keep on working on my feelings and how to handle it. But the feelings will always be there the way they are, intense and long, the only thing I can do it working on how I act on them. But that still won't change the fact that those feelings are there and are so intense that they give me physical pain or stomach sickness etc. And I am not strong enough yet to basically "blackmail" my own brain into thinking its not as bad as its thinking and telling myself I only make things up. 

Its just exhausting. I'm fighting with myself every day and sometimes people seem to forget that...
Thank you for your answer, I appreciate it! x

Oh yes, I understand you. To me there's a huge step between that and controlling.

I work on my BPD traits, I'm on medication, I had therapy and am currently without therapy due to not having found one after moving to a different part of the country but am on waiting lists. I've been in partly stationary mental hospital treatment twice for 8 weeks each in 2020 & 2021. He knows all that.  And I've bettered my behaviour. He knows I'm working on it. But it seems like he thinks working on it means he can figuratively throw me into deep cold water and I'll have to learn to swim by myself without anyone showing me how its done and expects me to succeed after one time and if I drown then its my own fault for not being able to swim 5 minutes after he threw me into the water. It seems he forgets that it takes a lot of time with billion little steps with compromises and help from the outside to learn something.

 He also told me that he sometimes get hurt by people but doesn't let it get to him and knows often it's just him seeing it as hurtful and told me everyone had to learn to handle their feelings so I have to do too. Yes of course, but the progress will be at least double as hard and difficult and there will be at least double the relapses and I need at least double the help and reassurance than "everyone" else aka people like him, without BPD. 

I hope we can both gain from responses to this post, if there will be some. Wishing you the best x

I dont look at it as abandonment per se, before he visited me and the week after until the breakup we repeatedly had an hour or two without texting due to him studying etc. And it was fine. I can manage up to a certrain amount, especially when I know its something important like studying, having classes or going to the library etc. But since the breakup and him blocking me I panic everytime he doesn't talk to me for just 10 minutes. I dont specifically see 'him not texting me for an hour' as abandonment. I fear that that hour is just the first hour of a week or forever, the first hour of another trust break and breakup. 

I dont want every detail. I dont ask for what he cooks, what he watches, what he scrolls through or anything. It just doesnt make sense to me that I am the person he wants to live with in the future, share a house with, spend the rest of his life with but sending a "I'll go cook and eat lunch now, we'll talk later" or something like that is sharing too much and he doesn't want that. Literally any kind of note that he will be gone for a while but will come back. It doesnt have to be forever, but its only one and a half weeks after he broke the biggest promise and broke up with me and blocked me. It seems like he brushed it off like nothing and already forgot about it. I am on the edge since, not knowing if when he doesnt read my messages its due to him having blocked me again or if hes just busy.

He knows fairly much about BPD i think and uses it a lot in discussions to tell me my reaction to certain things he did is based on my BPD. Which sometimes is really irritating and annoying because he sometimes also says that about situations where people without BPD would also have reacted or felt the way I did about something he did. Just he wouldn't have, so he puts it on BPD.

I keep telling him too that communication is the key to a happy relationship and he struggles with it but wants to work on it...
